syllabusStandard.isolationRule: Formulas are scoped strictly by board + class + syllabusYear. Do not reuse higher-class formulas in lower classes.

formulas.subject: Arithmetic
formulas.name: nth Odd Number

variables.meaning: Position of the term (natural number, n ≥ 1)

formulas.description: Odd numbers form the sequence 1, 3, 5, 7, … The nth odd number is obtained by doubling n and subtracting 1.
formulas.example: Find the 8th odd number. a_8 = 2×8 − 1 = 16 − 1 = 15. So the 8th odd number is 15.
formulas.notes: Class 6 pattern rule only — not an algebraic identity of higher classes.

practiceQuestions.question: Which position has the odd number 21?

source.chapterReference: Class 6 Mathematics — Chapter 1: Patterns in Mathematics

formulas.subject: Arithmetic
formulas.name: nth Even Number
formulas.description: Even numbers form the sequence 2, 4, 6, 8, … The nth even number is twice n.
formulas.example: Find the 9th even number. a_9 = 2×9 = 18.
formulas.notes: For n = 1, the first even counting number in this pattern is taken as 2.

source.chapterReference: Class 6 Mathematics — Chapter 1: Patterns in Mathematics

formulas.subject: Arithmetic
formulas.name: nth Triangular Number

variables.meaning: Position / number of rows in the triangle pattern

formulas.description: Triangular numbers count dots arranged in a triangular pattern: 1, 3, 6, 10, 15, …
formulas.notes: This is a Class 6 pattern formula, not a mensuration area formula.

source.chapterReference: Class 6 Mathematics — Chapter 1: Patterns in Mathematics

formulas.subject: Arithmetic
formulas.name: nth Square Number
formulas.description: Square numbers are 1, 4, 9, 16, 25, … obtained by multiplying a number by itself.
formulas.example: Find the 6th square number. S_6 = 6² = 36.

source.chapterReference: Class 6 Mathematics — Chapter 1: Patterns in Mathematics

formulas.subject: Arithmetic
formulas.name: nth Cube Number
formulas.description: Cube numbers are 1, 8, 27, 64, … obtained by multiplying a number by itself three times.
formulas.example: Find the 4th cube number. C_4 = 4³ = 64.
formulas.notes: Cube numbers as patterns only; solid volume formulas belong to higher classes.

source.chapterReference: Class 6 Mathematics — Chapter 1: Patterns in Mathematics

formulas.subject: Arithmetic
formulas.name: Fibonacci Sequence Rule
formulas.description: Each Fibonacci number is the sum of the two numbers before it: 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13, …
formulas.notes: Starting values may be shown as 1, 1 or 0, 1 depending on convention.

source.chapterReference: Class 6 Mathematics — Chapter 1: Patterns in Mathematics

formulas.subject: Arithmetic
formulas.name: Place Value of a Digit
formulas.formula: Place value = digit × value of its place
formulas.description: The place value of a digit depends on its position in the number (ones, tens, hundreds, …).
formulas.example: In 4,582 the place value of 5 is 5 × 100 = 500.
formulas.notes: Face value of a digit is the digit itself; place value depends on position.

source.chapterReference: Class 6 Mathematics — Chapter 3: Number Play

formulas.subject: Arithmetic
formulas.name: Expanded Form of a Number
formulas.formula: Number = sum of (each digit × its place value)
formulas.description: Expanded form writes a number as the sum of the place values of its digits.

source.chapterReference: Class 6 Mathematics — Chapter 3: Number Play

formulas.subject: Arithmetic
formulas.name: Factor Relation
formulas.formula: If a is a factor of b, then b = a × k for some whole number k
formulas.description: A factor of a number divides it exactly, leaving no remainder.
formulas.example: 4 is a factor of 20 because 20 = 4 × 5.
formulas.notes: 1 is a factor of every whole number; every number is a factor of itself.

source.chapterReference: Class 6 Mathematics — Chapter 5: Prime Time

formulas.subject: Arithmetic
formulas.name: Multiple Relation
formulas.description: Multiples of a number are obtained by multiplying it by 1, 2, 3, …
formulas.example: Multiples of 5 include 5, 10, 15, 20, …

practiceQuestions.question: Write the first four multiples of 8.

source.chapterReference: Class 6 Mathematics — Chapter 5: Prime Time

formulas.subject: Arithmetic
formulas.name: Divisibility Rule for 2
formulas.formula: A number is divisible by 2 if its ones digit is 0, 2, 4, 6 or 8
formulas.description: Even numbers are exactly the numbers divisible by 2.
formulas.example: 148 ends with 8, so 148 is divisible by 2.

source.chapterReference: Class 6 Mathematics — Chapter 5: Prime Time

formulas.subject: Arithmetic
formulas.name: Divisibility Rule for 3
formulas.formula: A number is divisible by 3 if the sum of its digits is divisible by 3

variables.meaning: Total obtained by adding all digits

formulas.description: Check divisibility by 3 without long division.
formulas.example: For 252: 2+5+2=9, and 9 is divisible by 3, so 252 is divisible by 3.
formulas.notes: You may repeatedly sum digits until a single digit remains.

source.chapterReference: Class 6 Mathematics — Chapter 5: Prime Time

formulas.subject: Arithmetic
formulas.name: Divisibility Rule for 5
formulas.formula: A number is divisible by 5 if its ones digit is 0 or 5
formulas.description: Numbers ending in 0 or 5 are divisible by 5.
formulas.example: 680 ends with 0, so it is divisible by 5.

source.chapterReference: Class 6 Mathematics — Chapter 5: Prime Time

formulas.subject: Arithmetic
formulas.name: Divisibility Rule for 9
formulas.formula: A number is divisible by 9 if the sum of its digits is divisible by 9

variables.meaning: Sum of all digits of the number

formulas.description: Similar to the rule for 3, but the digit sum must be divisible by 9.
formulas.example: For 729: 7+2+9=18, and 18 is divisible by 9, so 729 is divisible by 9.

source.chapterReference: Class 6 Mathematics — Chapter 5: Prime Time

formulas.subject: Arithmetic
formulas.name: Divisibility Rule for 10
formulas.formula: A number is divisible by 10 if its ones digit is 0
formulas.description: A number ending with 0 is divisible by 10.
formulas.example: 940 ends with 0, so it is divisible by 10.

source.chapterReference: Class 6 Mathematics — Chapter 5: Prime Time

formulas.subject: Arithmetic
formulas.name: HCF × LCM Relation (Two Numbers)
formulas.formula: HCF(a, b) × LCM(a, b) = a × b
formulas.description: For any two positive integers, the product of their HCF and LCM equals the product of the numbers.
formulas.notes: This relation is stated for two numbers.

source.chapterReference: Class 6 Mathematics — Chapter 5: Prime Time

formulas.subject: Arithmetic
formulas.name: Fraction Notation
formulas.description: A fraction represents equal parts of a whole.
formulas.example: 3 equal slices out of 8 give the fraction 3/8.
formulas.notes: Denominator cannot be zero.

practiceQuestions.question: What fraction is 5 shaded squares out of 12?

source.chapterReference: Class 6 Mathematics — Chapter 7: Fractions

formulas.subject: Arithmetic
formulas.name: Equivalent Fractions
formulas.formula: a/b = (a × k)/(b × k) for any natural number k
formulas.description: Multiplying numerator and denominator by the same non-zero number gives an equivalent fraction.

source.chapterReference: Class 6 Mathematics — Chapter 7: Fractions

formulas.subject: Arithmetic
formulas.name: Addition of Like Fractions
formulas.description: When denominators are the same, add the numerators and keep the denominator.
formulas.notes: For unlike fractions, first make denominators equal.

source.chapterReference: Class 6 Mathematics — Chapter 7: Fractions

formulas.subject: Arithmetic
formulas.name: Subtraction of Like Fractions
formulas.description: When denominators are the same, subtract the numerators and keep the denominator.

source.chapterReference: Class 6 Mathematics — Chapter 7: Fractions

formulas.subject: Arithmetic
formulas.name: Improper Fraction to Mixed Number
formulas.formula: a/b = q + r/b, where a = q×b + r
formulas.description: Divide numerator by denominator; quotient is the whole part and remainder forms the fractional part.
formulas.example: 17/5 = 3 + 2/5, because 17 = 3×5 + 2 (mixed number: 3 2/5).

source.chapterReference: Class 6 Mathematics — Chapter 7: Fractions

formulas.subject: Arithmetic
formulas.name: Absolute Value
formulas.formula: |a| = distance of a from 0 on the number line
formulas.description: Absolute value measures how far a number is from zero, ignoring direction.
formulas.notes: Absolute value is never negative.

source.chapterReference: Class 6 Mathematics — Chapter 10: The Other Side of Zero

ncertReference.chapter: Chapter 10: The Other Side of Zero

formulas.subject: Arithmetic
formulas.name: Additive Inverse
formulas.description: Every integer has an opposite that sums with it to zero.
formulas.example: The additive inverse of 9 is −9 because 9+(−9)=0.
formulas.notes: The additive inverse of 0 is 0.

practiceQuestions.question: What is the additive inverse of −4?

source.chapterReference: Class 6 Mathematics — Chapter 10: The Other Side of Zero

ncertReference.chapter: Chapter 10: The Other Side of Zero

formulas.subject: Arithmetic
formulas.name: Integer Addition on the Number Line
formulas.formula: Add +k → move k units right; add −k → move k units left

variables.meaning: Positive number of units to move

formulas.description: Integer addition can be modelled by moves on the number line.
formulas.example: Start at 3; add −5 → move 5 left → −2. So 3+(−5)=−2.
formulas.notes: Class 6 emphasises number-line understanding of integer operations.

source.chapterReference: Class 6 Mathematics — Chapter 10: The Other Side of Zero

ncertReference.chapter: Chapter 10: The Other Side of Zero

formulas.subject: Geometry
formulas.name: Right Angle
formulas.description: An angle that measures exactly 90° is a right angle.
formulas.example: The corner of a square page is a right angle (90°).
formulas.notes: Acute < 90°, obtuse between 90° and 180°.

source.chapterReference: Class 6 Mathematics — Chapter 2: Lines and Angles

formulas.subject: Geometry
formulas.name: Straight Angle
formulas.description: An angle that forms a straight line measures 180°.
formulas.example: A straight angle looks like a straight line and measures 180°.

source.chapterReference: Class 6 Mathematics — Chapter 2: Lines and Angles

formulas.subject: Geometry
formulas.name: Complete Angle
formulas.description: A complete angle is one full rotation about a point.
formulas.example: Turning fully around to the same direction is a 360° turn.

practiceQuestions.question: How many right angles make one complete angle?

source.chapterReference: Class 6 Mathematics — Chapter 2: Lines and Angles

formulas.subject: Geometry
formulas.name: Complementary Angles
formulas.description: Two angles are complementary if their measures sum to 90°.
formulas.example: If ∠A = 35°, complement = 90° − 35° = 55°.
formulas.notes: Complementary angles need not be adjacent.

source.chapterReference: Class 6 Mathematics — Chapter 2: Lines and Angles

formulas.subject: Geometry
formulas.name: Supplementary Angles
formulas.description: Two angles are supplementary if their measures sum to 180°.
formulas.notes: Angles on a straight line are supplementary.

source.chapterReference: Class 6 Mathematics — Chapter 2: Lines and Angles

formulas.subject: Geometry
formulas.name: Circle Defined by Radius
formulas.formula: A circle is the set of all points at fixed distance r from centre O
formulas.description: With compass and ruler, a circle is drawn by keeping a constant radius from the centre.
formulas.example: If radius is 4 cm, every point on the circle is 4 cm from the centre.
formulas.notes: Class 6 focuses on construction; π-based circumference depth belongs later.

practiceQuestions.question: If OP = 5 cm for every point P on a circle with centre O, find radius.

source.chapterReference: Class 6 Mathematics — Chapter 8: Playing with Constructions

formulas.subject: Geometry
formulas.name: Perpendicular Bisector Property
formulas.formula: Any point on the perpendicular bisector of AB is equidistant from A and B
formulas.latex: PA=PB\text{ for }P\text{ on the perpendicular bisector of }AB
formulas.description: The perpendicular bisector meets a segment at its midpoint at 90° and is the locus of equidistant points.
formulas.example: If M is midpoint of AB and line l ⊥ AB at M, then for any P on l, PA = PB.

practiceQuestions.question: Where does the perpendicular bisector meet AB?

source.chapterReference: Class 6 Mathematics — Chapter 8: Playing with Constructions

formulas.subject: Geometry
formulas.name: Line of Symmetry
formulas.formula: A line of symmetry divides a figure into two mirror-image halves
formulas.latex: \text{reflection across }\ell\text{ maps the figure onto itself}
formulas.description: If one half of a figure is the mirror image of the other across a line, that line is a line of symmetry.
formulas.example: A square has 4 lines of symmetry; a non-equilateral isosceles triangle has 1.
formulas.notes: Some figures have no line of symmetry.

practiceQuestions.question: How many lines of symmetry does an equilateral triangle have?

source.chapterReference: Class 6 Mathematics — Chapter 9: Symmetry

formulas.subject: Geometry
formulas.name: Order of Rotational Symmetry
formulas.formula: Order = 360° ÷ (smallest angle of rotation that maps the figure onto itself)

variables.meaning: Smallest positive rotation angle of symmetry
Number of matching positions in one full turn

formulas.description: Rotational symmetry exists when a figure looks the same after a turn less than 360° about its centre.
formulas.example: A square matches every 90°, so order = 360/90 = 4.
formulas.notes: Every figure has order at least 1.

practiceQuestions.question: A regular hexagon matches every 60°. Find its order.

source.chapterReference: Class 6 Mathematics — Chapter 9: Symmetry

formulas.subject: Mensuration
formulas.name: Perimeter of a Rectangle
formulas.description: Perimeter is the total boundary length. A rectangle has two lengths and two breadths.
formulas.example: If l=12 cm and b=5 cm, P=2(12+5)=34 cm.
formulas.notes: Perimeter units are units of length.

practiceQuestions.question: Perimeter of a 9 m by 4 m rectangle?

source.chapterReference: Class 6 Mathematics — Chapter 6: Perimeter and Area

formulas.subject: Mensuration
formulas.name: Perimeter of a Square
formulas.description: All four sides of a square are equal, so perimeter is four times one side.
formulas.example: If a=6 cm, P=4×6=24 cm.

source.chapterReference: Class 6 Mathematics — Chapter 6: Perimeter and Area

formulas.subject: Mensuration
formulas.name: Perimeter of a Triangle
formulas.description: The perimeter of a triangle is the sum of its three sides.
formulas.example: Sides 3 cm, 4 cm, 5 cm ⇒ P=12 cm.

practiceQuestions.question: Perimeter of sides 7 cm, 8 cm, 9 cm?

source.chapterReference: Class 6 Mathematics — Chapter 6: Perimeter and Area

formulas.subject: Mensuration
formulas.name: Area of a Rectangle
formulas.description: Area measures the enclosed region. For a rectangle, area is length times breadth.
formulas.example: If l=10 cm and b=4 cm, A=40 cm².
formulas.notes: Area units are square units. Perimeter and area are independent measures.

practiceQuestions.question: Area of a 15 m by 6 m rectangle?

source.chapterReference: Class 6 Mathematics — Chapter 6: Perimeter and Area

formulas.subject: Mensuration
formulas.name: Area of a Square
formulas.description: Area of a square is the side multiplied by itself.
formulas.example: If a=9 cm, A=81 cm².
formulas.notes: A larger perimeter does not always mean a larger area.

practiceQuestions.question: Side 12 m. Find area of the square.

source.chapterReference: Class 6 Mathematics — Chapter 6: Perimeter and Area

formulas.subject: Data Handling
formulas.name: Frequency
formulas.formula: Frequency of an item = number of times it occurs in the data
formulas.description: Tally marks help count how often each value appears; that count is the frequency.
formulas.example: In {2,3,2,2,5}, frequency of 2 is 3.
formulas.notes: Tally marks are usually grouped in fives.

source.chapterReference: Class 6 Mathematics — Chapter 4: Data Handling and Presentation

formulas.subject: Data Handling
formulas.name: Pictograph Scale
formulas.formula: Actual value = (number of symbols) × (value of one symbol)
formulas.description: In a pictograph, each picture stands for a fixed number of items according to the scale.
formulas.example: If 1 symbol = 10 students and 4 symbols are shown, value = 40.
formulas.notes: Always read the key/scale before interpreting.

source.chapterReference: Class 6 Mathematics — Chapter 4: Data Handling and Presentation

formulas.subject: Data Handling
formulas.name: Bar Graph Reading
formulas.formula: Value = (bar height in axis units) × (scale of the axis)
formulas.description: A bar graph uses bars of equal width; bar length represents the value for each category.
formulas.example: If scale is 1 unit = 5 and bar reaches 6 units, value = 30.
formulas.notes: Bars should be equally spaced with clear labels.

practiceQuestions.question: Scale 1 cm = 2 goals. Bar height 9 cm. Goals?

source.chapterReference: Class 6 Mathematics — Chapter 4: Data Handling and Presentation
